name: SPAIN

flag.title: Flag of Spain
flag.note: Red & yellow stripes, coat of arms

lead: Spain is at the western tip of Europe. It has blazing sunshine, old castles and very loud festivals. Matadors, tapas and siestas are real. So are high-speed trains over 300 km/h.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Highest capital city in the EU

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Spain is mostly a high, flat plateau called the Meseta. The Pyrenees form a wall between Spain and France. The Sierra Nevada rises near Granada.
Three seas lap its shores: the Atlantic, the Mediterranean and the Bay of Biscay. Spain also owns the Canary Islands and the Balearic Islands, Mallorca and Ibiza.
animals: The Doñana wetlands shelter the Iberian lynx, the world's rarest wild cat. People rescued it from near-extinction (almost vanishing). Iberian wolves still roam the northern hills in small packs.
Brown bears lumber through the Cantabrian mountains. Huge griffon vultures circle the gorges of Extremadura. In autumn, red deer stags bellow in a noisy contest called the berrea.
culture: Spain runs on a different clock. Lunch is the big meal, at 2 to 3 pm. Dinner rarely starts before 9 pm. The word tapas once meant bread placed on a glass to keep flies out.
Flamenco mixes clapping, guitar and stamping dance. It was born in Andalusia. Pamplona runs bulls through its streets. Valencia burns giant wooden sculptures every March.
history: Muslim rulers called the Moors held parts of Spain for nearly 800 years. Palaces like the Alhambra still stand. In 1492, the year Columbus sailed west, the last Moorish kingdom fell.
Spain then built a vast empire across the Americas and Asia. A brutal civil war came in the 1930s. Afterwards Spain became a democracy. It joined the EU in 1986.
wows: At La Tomatina each August, 20,000 people hurl 150 tonnes of tomatoes.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.
Spain has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than almost any other country.
Madrid's Prado Museum holds over 8,000 paintings.
A Spaniard, Manuel Jalón Corominas, patented the modern mop in 1956.
Spanish is the world's second most spoken native language, with 490 million speakers.
Spain's AVE high-speed rail network is Europe's longest, at over 3,900 km.

myths.myth: Spain is always hot and sunny
myths.fact: Not in the north. Galicia and the Basque Country are rainy and green.

myths.myth: Bulls charge because of the red
myths.fact: Bulls are colourblind to red. The moving cloth excites them, not its colour.
